## Problem1
I simulated birthdays as independent draws from 365 equally likely days. The function below returns `TRUE` if at least two people share a birthday and `FALSE` otherwise.
```{r p1_function}
simulate_birthday = function(group_size) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = group_size, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}
```
```{r p1_simulation}
set.seed(1)

birthday_results =
  tibble(group_size = 2:50) |>
  mutate(
    shared_birthday = map(
      group_size,
      \(n) map_lgl(
        seq_len(10000),
        \(iteration) simulate_birthday(group_size = n)
      )
    ),
    probability = map_dbl(shared_birthday, mean)
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(birthday_results) == 49,
  all(lengths(birthday_results$shared_birthday) == 10000),
  all(birthday_results$probability >= 0),
  all(birthday_results$probability <= 1)
)
```
```{r p1_plot}
birthday_results |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#0072B2") +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, color = "#0072B2") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2, 10, 20, 23, 30, 40, 50)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
    labels = scales::label_percent()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Shared birthdays become more likely as the group grows",
    subtitle = "10,000 simulated groups at each group size",
    x = "Number of people in the group",
    y = "Probability of at least one shared birthday"
  )
```

For each group size, I averaged the results of 10,000 simulations. The estimated probability of a shared birthday is `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * birthday_results$probability[birthday_results$group_size == 23])` for 23 people and `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * birthday_results$probability[birthday_results$group_size == 50])` for 50 people. The probability rises quickly because the number of pairs of people increases with group size. A group of 23 people already contains 253 possible pairs, so a shared birthday is fairly likely even though there are 365 possible birthdays.

## Problem2
```{r p2_import}
subject_files =
  tibble(
    file_path = list.files(
      "data",
      pattern = "^(con|exp)_[0-9]{2}\\.csv$",
      full.names = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    file_name = basename(file_path),
    data = map(
      file_path,
      \(path) read_csv(
        path,
        col_types = cols(.default = col_double()),
        show_col_types = FALSE
      )
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(subject_files) == 20,
  all(map_int(subject_files$data, nrow) == 1),
  all(map_int(subject_files$data, ncol) == 8)
)
```

```{r p2_tidy}
study_df =
  subject_files |>
  select(file_name, data) |>
  unnest(cols = data) |>
  mutate(participant_id = str_remove(file_name, "\\.csv$")) |>
  separate(
    participant_id,
    into = c("arm", "subject_id"),
    sep = "_",
    remove = FALSE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    arm = factor(
      arm,
      levels = c("con", "exp"),
      labels = c("Control", "Experimental")
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    names_transform = list(week = as.integer),
    values_to = "observation"
  ) |>
  select(participant_id, subject_id, arm, week, observation) |>
  arrange(arm, subject_id, week)

stopifnot(
  nrow(study_df) == 160,
  n_distinct(study_df$participant_id) == 20,
  all(count(study_df, participant_id)$n == 8),
  all(count(study_df, participant_id, week)$n == 1),
  !anyNA(study_df),
  identical(sort(unique(study_df$week)), 1:8)
)
```
I first created a dataframe of file names and used `map()` to read each participant's observations into a list column. I then expanded the list column, extracted the arm and subject ID, and converted the eight weekly columns to long format. The tidy dataset contains `r nrow(study_df)` observations from `r n_distinct(study_df$participant_id)` participants followed for eight weeks. Each row represents one participant at one week. Subject IDs are repeated across arms, so `participant_id` combines the arm and subject ID to identify each person uniquely.
```{r p2_summary}
arm_summary =
  study_df |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    participants = n_distinct(participant_id),
    week_1_mean = mean(observation[week == 1]),
    week_8_mean = mean(observation[week == 8]),
    mean_change = week_8_mean - week_1_mean,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  arm_summary,
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Arm", "Participants", "Week 1 mean", "Week 8 mean", "Mean change"
  ),
  caption = "Observed values at the first and last weeks by study arm"
)
```
```{r p2_plot}
study_df |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = week,
      y = observation,
      group = participant_id,
      color = arm
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.75, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ arm, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Control = "#0072B2", Experimental = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly observations for each participant",
    subtitle = "Each line follows one participant; panels use the same y scale",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Observed value"
  )
```

The experimental group shows an overall upward pattern, while observations in the control group fluctuate around a more stable level. The experimental group mean increases from `r sprintf("%.2f", arm_summary$week_1_mean[arm_summary$arm == "Experimental"])` in week 1 to `r sprintf("%.2f", arm_summary$week_8_mean[arm_summary$arm == "Experimental"])` in week 8. The corresponding control group means are `r sprintf("%.2f", arm_summary$week_1_mean[arm_summary$arm == "Control"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", arm_summary$week_8_mean[arm_summary$arm == "Control"])`. Individual trajectories vary in both groups, but the separation between groups is clearer by the later weeks.
